missing_policy_citation.requirement_source: SPEC.md RESP-1 ("Cite the policy identifier for every claim derived from a policy document")
missing_policy_citation.evaluator_type: Needs tool-result ground truth: requires knowing which policy_id was actually retrieved/applicable (from get_policy/search_help_center results), not just pattern-matching the reply text.

ignores_data_quality_anomaly.definition: Agent fails to escalate a data-quality anomaly -- a missing required field (e.g. a null delivery date) or an inconsistent/unreconciled field (e.g. mismatched store/product, an impossible ship-after-deliver date order, an invalid negative price) -- instead treating the record as trustworthy enough to answer from directly. Hedging alone (flagging the anomaly in the reply without calling escalate_to_human) is not sufficient by itself -- escalation is the required corrective action. Reconciling the underlying data itself is out of scope for the agent.
example_quotes: Did not identify data discrepancy.
This has a specification gap because there is no tool or way for the agent to know there's a product/store mismatch.
this order lists a product that does not belong to the listed store
agent assumed all returned products with the same title belonged to the same store without checking store identifiers.

ignores_data_quality_anomaly.requirement_source: SPEC.md RESP-3 ("State when required information is missing or inconsistent, rather than inventing a value") + the seeded data_quality_cases table as ground truth for which records are damaged.
ignores_data_quality_anomaly.evaluator_type: Objectively checkable from the tool-call trace alone: does the order/product match a known data_quality_cases entry, and was escalate_to_human called. No text-quality judgment needed.

leaks_internal_terminology.definition: Agent surfaces raw internal field/variable names (e.g. refund_eligible) to the customer rather than translating them into plain language. Citing a policy id (RESP-1) is not itself a violation of this mode.

leaks_internal_terminology.evaluator_type: Checkable from reply text alone against a known list of internal field/variable names (refund_eligible, store_id, user_id, product_id, etc.); citing a policy id is explicitly not a violation.

continues_past_refusal.definition: After correctly declining an out-of-scope request, the agent continues on to offer further suggestions rather than stopping cleanly.
example_quotes: This agent should have stopped after declining the request and not have continued to give suggestions
close_negative_notes: support-0166: same trace -- clean, single-line decline with no unsolicited continuation.
continues_past_refusal.requirement_source: SPEC.md SCOPE-2 (refusal cases) + the system prompt's refusal-rules section ("Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences").
continues_past_refusal.evaluator_type: Checkable from reply text alone, but requires judgment on where "cleanly stopping" ends and "continuing" begins -- not a bright-line rule.

inefficient_tool_use.definition: Agent makes many near-duplicate or speculative tool calls (e.g. guessing individual product names one at a time) instead of the one obviously-sufficient call available to it (e.g. a broad query with the right filters), even when the eventual answer is correct. The failure is the wasted calls/latency, independent of final-answer correctness.
example_quotes: Very inefficient tool use: 10 near-duplicate search_products calls guessing individual product names/prices before trying the obvious broad query
It denied the refund correctly but made unnecessary tool calls
Answered correctly but made unnecessary tool calls
3 search_products calls with varying phrasing/params before landing on a working query, plus 2 get_store_info calls for the same store
3 search_products calls with varying phrasing/params, plus 2 get_store_info calls trying different store identifier formats
close_negative_notes: support-0152: 4 distinct tool calls (get_order, search_help_center, get_policy, escalate_to_human), each genuinely necessary for a dispute case, no redundancy.
support-0153: same shape, same justified multi-call pattern.
inefficient_tool_use.requirement_source: No SPEC.md id -- a human-judgment quality concern (call efficiency), not a written requirement.
inefficient_tool_use.evaluator_type: Needs the full tool-call sequence, not just the final reply -- counts/compares calls for redundancy against the obviously-sufficient alternative.

no_clarifying_question.definition: Agent acts on an ambiguous/under-specified request -- either guessing a specific record or providing everything (e.g. the full order list) -- instead of asking the shopper a clarifying question first.

support-0195: same duplicate-title case, same correct clarifying behavior.
no_clarifying_question.requirement_source: No single SPEC.md id -- recurring human_judgment criteria across individual scenarios' expected.criterion fields (e.g. support-0230), not one fixed numbered requirement.
no_clarifying_question.evaluator_type: Needs ground truth about actual ambiguity (how many records genuinely match) plus the reply text -- can't be judged from the reply alone.

asks_for_unusable_information.definition: Agent asks the customer for information that no available tool can accept or use (a product link/URL, a SKU, a screenshot, or a 'store location' concept not part of this platform), even as just one option alongside a usable one, instead of using the tools it actually has or asking only for something a tool could act on. Offering an unusable option is a violation on its own -- it doesn't need to be the only option offered.
example_quotes: there's no tool that takes store location like this
this was irrelevant and presented as a non-actionable next step
should not ask for purchase date
asks whether to check a specific "store/location," a concept not part of this platform
asks the customer to share a link to the product page after escalating
offers "paste the product link/name" -- product link is unusable even though name is a real option
offers "share a link/screenshot" alongside "which option/store" -- unusable option offered regardless
close_negative_notes: support-0245: find_order returns no matches, so the agent asks for the order number or store name -- both real, usable tool parameters -- instead of a link/SKU/screenshot.
asks_for_unusable_information.requirement_source: SPEC.md section 4 (Tools) -- the input signatures of TOOL-1 through TOOL-9 define what a tool can actually accept; this mode is a direct implementation-contract check, not a narrative requirement.
asks_for_unusable_information.evaluator_type: Objectively checkable given the tool signatures: does any available tool accept the thing being asked for. No fuzzy judgment once the tool contracts are known.

fails_to_refuse_out_of_scope.definition: Agent engages with or attempts to help an out-of-scope request (unrelated to Cartwheel -- e.g. a recipe, a third-party marketplace order) instead of declining it. Distinct from continues_past_refusal, which assumes the agent did refuse first and only over-continues afterward.
example_quotes: Agent provided recipe for banana bread instead of declining the out of scope request
Agent did not capture the user request about Amazon order and assumed it was for Cartwheel. Agent should've declined out of scope request.
Agent shoudln't have offered to do anything that has nothing to do with Cartwheel
close_negative_notes: support-0166: "help me file my taxes" -- declines cleanly in one line, does not continue past it.
fails_to_refuse_out_of_scope.requirement_source: SPEC.md SCOPE-2 ("The agent refuses: legal advice, payment-credential handling, anything outside Cartwheel").
fails_to_refuse_out_of_scope.evaluator_type: Checkable from reply text alone: did the agent decline, or did it attempt to help with the out-of-scope request.

escalation_handling_failure.definition: Agent's escalation handling doesn't match what the situation requires: either offers an escalation channel that doesn't fit the actual denial (e.g. suggesting a dispute for a policy-window override, or offering to 'check access' for a permanent authorization boundary), or never escalates a case the spec requires escalating (e.g. a dispute under ESC-3), giving only in-house guidance instead with no channel offered at all.
example_quotes: Agent should not have offered to open a dispute
Offered to help with the order the user was not supposed to have access to
Agent did not escalate to human
Agent should've escalated to human
Agent should've escalated to human
close_negative_notes: support-0152: dispute (ESC-3) on order 3677; agent calls escalate_to_human directly, no wrong-channel offer, no stalling.
support-0153: same dispute shape (order 1023), same correct direct escalation.
support-0159 live-chat continuation: asks for confirmation first, then correctly calls escalate_to_human once confirmed -- completes the accepted "ask first" pattern.
escalation_handling_failure.requirement_source: SPEC.md ESC-1 through ESC-4 (which case requires escalation) + RESP-4 (explaining escalations correctly).
escalation_handling_failure.evaluator_type: Needs the tool-call trace (was escalate_to_human called) plus ground truth on which ESC-* rule applies to this case -- not judgable from reply text alone.
